seams.what: the persistent editor chrome where a Blender-like File entry can be reached
seams.evidence: the top bar is always visible, while object-specific actions live in the sidebar and viewport tools live on the left shelf
seams.asks: should file actions live in a Blender-style File menu, as separate top-bar buttons, or in editor settings?

seams.what: the only frontend composition point that may wire DOM modules and live scene state together
seams.evidence: Connect and the texture inspector both expose attach functions and are composed here; export scope needs current selection and file actions need status reporting
seams.asks: should import/export status stay in its dialog, enter the action log, or appear in both?

seams.what: the explicit unit-test discovery list required by this Windows Node setup
seams.evidence: frontend/CLAUDE.md states every new *.test.js must be imported here or npm run test:frontend silently skips it
seams.asks: no product choice; this seam will wire the file-flow tests into the required suite

seams.what: the real-browser journey suite where file picker, download, focus, and dialog behavior can be verified
seams.evidence: Connect and gizmo browser journeys are registered from this single smoke-test entry point
seams.asks: should completed exports automatically download, or show a ready row that the user clicks?

seams.what: the same-origin upload/download boundary used by the static editor
seams.evidence: texture uploads already use bounded POST bodies and managed temporary files here; client setup and texture assets use named allowlisted routes
seams.asks: which formats and maximum upload size should the editor accept, and should multi-file formats arrive as a bundle?

seams.anchor: def serve_frontend(port: int, directory: Path) -> http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer:
seams.what: the point where the HTTP server must receive a safe capability for the live scene instead of only a static directory
seams.evidence: serve_frontend currently exposes only managed_texture_root; import needs the running orchestrator/scene and export needs the engine
seams.asks: must imports require the build to be paused, while exports remain available during a run?

seams.what: the live graph holding engine, scene, orchestrator, registry, and viewer references
seams.evidence: opening a native project may replace scene state and must keep all five references coherent; importing an asset can use the existing scene
seams.asks: should Open replace the current project in-place while keeping the agent/browser session connected, or restart the live session?

seams.what: the frozen engine boundary that currently exposes GLB/glTF export but no import capability
seams.evidence: all non-Blender code and the fake engine compile against EngineProtocol; Blender 5.2 locally exposes glTF, FBX, OBJ, PLY, STL, and USD import/export operators
seams.asks: which interchange formats belong in the supported public contract for this version?

seams.what: the concrete Blender engine composition where file-import behavior must become reachable
seams.evidence: BlenderEngine composes MeshOps, surfacing, and ExportingMixin; a new import responsibility must be mixed in here
seams.asks: on import, should hierarchy be flattened to world transforms and non-mesh objects be ignored with a report, or should hierarchy/cameras/lights be preserved?

seams.what: the bpy-free engine implementation every backend and integration suite depends on
seams.evidence: it records the full export conversion today; import must gain deterministic fake behavior so the feature is testable without Blender
seams.asks: no product choice; the fake will mirror the chosen public import/export contract

seams.what: the existing export policy that checks geometry, applies target conversion, writes, and returns a warning report
seams.evidence: it always writes despite defects and currently delegates only export_gltf
seams.asks: should editor export keep the existing warn-and-continue policy, and should it export the current selection or the whole scene by default?

seams.what: the current agent export default, which converts metres to Roblox studs
seams.evidence: an editor Save/Export action using this default would unexpectedly rescale a generic GLB; Godot is currently the closest generic glTF profile but is not named that way
seams.asks: should the editor default to generic glTF metres with optional Roblox/Unity/Unreal/Godot profiles, or inherit Roblox?

seams.what: the public agent-facing file tool declarations
seams.evidence: export_scene and check_export_budget are declared here, then rebound to live handlers without changing their schemas
seams.asks: should agents receive a matching import_scene_file tool, and should the existing export_scene schema gain a format option without breaking current calls?

seams.what: the direct MCP execution route for file operations that do not belong in the ordinary export log path
seams.evidence: export runs outside scene history because it mutates no geometry; import must instead enter shared history and report produced objects
seams.asks: may agents import any local path under the existing unrestricted-local trust model, while browser uploads remain managed and allowlisted?

seams.anchor: def build_handlers(*, include_raw: bool = True) -> HandlerRegistry:
seams.what: the replay registry every geometry-changing operation must reach
seams.evidence: browser edits and agent operations share this registry; an imported asset must be replayable or explicitly opaque to keep undo honest
seams.asks: should one import be one undo step, with the source copied into managed project storage so replay remains deterministic?

seams.what: the browser-originated write path that logs edits, takes a short lease, publishes reports, and keeps one shared history
seams.evidence: direct engine writes are explicitly rejected here as a second timeline; import from the editor has the same consequence
seams.asks: should import use this shared operation path and remain undoable, while Open Project deliberately replaces history after confirmation?

seams.what: the existing but UI-inaccessible forge3d JSON operation-log save/load capability
seams.evidence: save preserves operations, head, checkpoints, barriers, and metadata; load returns a new Scene and requires replay, while texture/import source assets are currently external paths
seams.asks: does 'the file' include a native editable forge3d project package, or only ordinary 3D interchange files?

seams.anchor: def capture(engine: EngineProtocol, path: str) -> str:
seams.what: the current all-geometry serializer used for undo barriers, including UVs and managed material definitions
seams.evidence: captures are temporary session files and deliberately not durable projects; a self-contained project package needs explicit asset packing rather than silently reusing temp paths
seams.asks: should native project files be self-contained packages with imported models and texture maps embedded, or reference files beside the project?

seams.what: the phase gate that currently makes EXPORT tools visible only during Polish
seams.evidence: a mutating import assigned only to the EXPORT role would be unavailable during Blockout, when bringing in reference or base geometry is most useful
seams.asks: in which phases should agents be allowed to import models, and should browser import be available whenever the operator pauses?

seams.what: the existing viewer path for export completion and warnings
seams.evidence: the frontend already handles EXPORT_REPORT, but the current MCP export handler never calls this method, so agent exports are invisible in the editor
seams.asks: should file completion and warnings appear in both the file dialog and action log for browser and agent exports?

dismissed.reason: no new WebSocket message is required if browser import uploads over same-origin HTTP and then uses the existing operator-edit operation path; export is a same-origin HTTP download
its resolver is deliberately image-only; scene file upload/download needs a separate allowlist and must not weaken the texture route
the browser already has File/Blob/download APIs and Python has zip/tempfile support; no runtime dependency is required
the product is a loopback-only local process with no accounts or database; visibility is controlled by local process access and MCP roles
